title: Postmortem: SEV-2 Console rollout UI bug triggered rollback loop (2026-02-22)
author: Ava Chen
customer_impact: Operators could not reliably pause or promote canary rollouts via Console. Some actions displayed as successful but were not applied, leading to confusion and delayed mitigations for unrelated rollouts.
summary: A Console UI change caused repeated client-side retries on a non-idempotent rollback endpoint, putting rollouts-service into a rollback loop for a subset of deployments.
timeline:
19:05 UTC: Internal user reported Console rollout controls unresponsive.
19:10 UTC: Eng on-call saw elevated 5xx and increased write QPS to rollouts-service.
19:20 UTC: Isolated to Console release 2026.02.22.2 with a new retry wrapper.
19:28 UTC: Disabled feature flag for retry wrapper in prod.
19:40 UTC: Rollouts-service write QPS returned to normal; rollback loops stopped.
19:58 UTC: Incident resolved.
root_cause: The Console’s new retry wrapper treated 409 conflict responses as retryable and retried POST /rollback automatically. The endpoint was not idempotent and could re-trigger rollback actions.
detection: Internal report and rollouts-service error/QPS alerts.
mitigation: Disabled the retry wrapper via feature flag and added a server-side idempotency key requirement for rollback actions.
what_went_well: Feature flag allowed immediate mitigation. Service-level alerts were actionable.
what_went_wrong: The UI change was not tested against the real rollouts-service conflict behavior; endpoint idempotency was assumed but not documented.
follow_ups: Document idempotency requirements for rollouts-service endpoints (Platform Engineering; due 2026-03-10).
Add integration tests in Console CI that simulate 409 and ensure no retries on non-idempotent endpoints (Console & Tooling; due 2026-03-15).
Introduce a standard client retry policy library with an allowlist of safe endpoints (DevEx; due 2026-04-01).
